CFML Language Reference: Functions

NumberFormat

Returns a number as a string, formatted according to a mask. Without a mask, the number is rounded to an integer and thousands separators are added.

Category

Display and formatting functions

Syntax

NumberFormat(number [, mask ])

Parameters

number
The number to format. An empty string is treated as zero.
mask
Characters that describe the format: 9 or _ digit placeholder (pads with spaces when the mask is wider than the number); 0 digit placeholder before the decimal point that pads with zeros; . decimal point (the number of placeholders after it sets the decimal places, with rounding); , thousands separators; L left-justify or C center within the width of the mask (right-justified is the default); - a space before positive numbers and a minus sign before negative ones; + a plus or minus sign; ( and ) parentheses around negative numbers; $ a dollar sign in front of the number.

Returns

The formatted number as a string.

Usage

The mask never truncates: if the number has more digits than the mask has placeholders, all of them are shown. The padding spaces only line up in a monospaced font, so display padded results inside <PRE> or <TT>.

The ^ character (separate formatting left and right of the decimal point) is accepted, but KoldFusion ignores it. DecimalFormat and DollarFormat are shortcuts for the two most common masks; LSNumberFormat formats numbers for the current locale.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<CFSET N = 1234.567>
<CFOUTPUT>
<PRE>
Mask           Result
(none)         [#NumberFormat(N)#]
9,999.99       [#NumberFormat(N, "9,999.99")#]
99999.9        [#NumberFormat(N, "99999.9")#]
L99999.9       [#NumberFormat(N, "L99999.9")#]
000000         [#NumberFormat(42, "000000")#]
$999,999.99    [#NumberFormat(N, "$999,999.99")#]
(9,999.99)     [#NumberFormat(-N, "(9,999.99)")#]
+9999          [#NumberFormat(42, "+9999")#]
-9999          [#NumberFormat(-42, "-9999")#]
</PRE>
</CFOUTPUT>
